title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: COVID-19 financial support schemes
sections.summary: MSF set up the National Care Hotline and disbursed $500 million through TRF, CSG and CRG, supporting around 470,000 individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: At MSF, we set up the National Care Hotline and rolled out key support schemes to protect individuals against income shocks and to meet their immediate needs, such as the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF) and COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG), where we disbursed a total of $440 million in assistance, supporting around 470,000 individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Subsequently, under the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG), we have disbursed around another $60 million so far; so, in total, $500 million.

sections.label: Housing grants for first-time buyers
sections.summary: Eligible first-time homebuyers can receive grants of up to $80,000 for new flats or up to $160,000 for resale flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, eligible first-time homebuyers can receive grants of up to $80,000 for new flats or up to $160,000 for resale flats – making public housing affordable.

sections.label: Education subsidies for Singaporean children
sections.summary: A Singaporean child can receive over $180,000 of education subsidies from preschool years until age 16.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, a Singaporean child can receive over $180,000 of education subsidies from the preschool years till the age of 16.

sections.label: Lifetime healthcare subsidies per Singaporean
sections.summary: The Government spends over $230,000 in healthcare subsidies for each Singaporean over their lifetime on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: On average, the Government spends over $230,000 in healthcare subsidies for each Singaporean over their lifetime.

sections.label: Workfare, ComCare, Silver Support, MediShield Life
sections.summary: Workfare and ComCare were rolled out, and Silver Support and MediShield Life were introduced as new features of the social security system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Workfare and ComCare were rolled out and new features of our social security system, like Silver Support and MediShield Life, were introduced.

sections.label: Training subsidies for ComCare recipients
sections.summary: In Budget 2022, training subsidies for ComCare recipients were expanded, cutting their costs from $10,000 to less than $1,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Because ultimately, we want them to bounce back together and stronger.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, in Budget 2022, to be even more enabling, we have also expanded training subsidies for ComCare recipients, making it easier for them to reskill and access good job opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Before subsidies, they would have to pay $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: After subsidies, they pay less than $1,000, which can be further offset to as little as to no cost, using their SkillsFuture Credit.

sections.label: Islandwide Social Service Offices network
sections.summary: From 2013 to 2015, an islandwide network of 24 Social Service Offices was set up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2015, we set up an islandwide network of 24 Social Service Offices, or SSOs.

sections.label: Marriage and divorce trends
sections.summary: Marriage rates declined over twenty years, couples have fewer children, and more recent marriage cohorts show a higher proportion of divorces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Marriage rates have declined over the past twenty years and couples are having fewer children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are also seeing a higher proportion of divorces among more recent marriage cohorts.

sections.label: Journey with You initiative pilot
sections.summary: The Journey with You (JOY) initiative is being piloted so couples may benefit from counsel from a trusted person.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The couple may then benefit from seeking counsel from a trusted person, who has journeyed with them from the start.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is why we are piloting the Journey with You (JOY) initiative.

sections.label: FAM@FSC support for families
sections.summary: FAM@FSC brings together marriage and divorce support programmes and family counselling, scaling up to 10 centres by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Next, for families showing early signs of stress, the Strengthening Families Programme @ Family Service Centre, or we shorten it to call it FAM@FSC, brings together marriage and divorce support programmes and family counselling to support them in a more integrated and accessible manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will scale up to 10 FAM@FSC centres by the end of the year.

sections.label: Family violence taskforce recommendations
sections.summary: The Government has accepted the 16 recommendations from the Taskforce on Family Violence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted the 16 recommendations from the Taskforce on Family Violence.

sections.label: MSFCare Network and donations
sections.summary: Community donations rose from about $1 billion in 2011 to over $1.5 billion in 2019, and the MSFCare Network was launched in January.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We especially want to encourage Singaporeans who have done well to give back to society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I was glad to know that community donations have increased over the past decade, from about $1 billion in 2011 to over $1.5 billion in 2019, coupled with a rise in volunteerism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I agree with Ms Denise Phua that we can help volunteers play a more active role in uplifting those with less.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, we launched the MSFCare Network in January, bringing together over 3,000 volunteers and partners across almost 80 volunteering opportunities under a single umbrella Network.

sections.label: Adoption of Children Act review
sections.summary: The Adoption of Children Act review studied global best practices, plans pre-adoption assessments and criminalising undesirable practices, and an Adoption of Children Bill this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the review of the Adoption of Children Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We studied best practices around the world and intend to adapt some of them for Singapore, such as mandating pre-adoption assessments and criminalising undesirable practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We plan to introduce the Adoption of Children Bill this year.

sections.label: Community Capability Trust funding
sections.summary: From April, SSAs can tap the Community Capability Trust to fund capability- and capacity-building efforts such as digitalisation or research and evaluation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: From April onwards, SSAs will be able to tap on the Community Capability Trust to fund their capability- and capacity-building efforts, for instance, in digitalisation or research and evaluation.

sections.label: Year of Celebrating SG Families
sections.summary: YCF will rally Singaporeans to celebrate families' role, encourage families to spend time together, and galvanise whole-of-society support for families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: YCF will rally Singaporeans to celebrate the important role that families play in our lives, encouraging families to spend time together and galvanise whole-of-society support for families.

sections.label: Celebrating SG Families Plan
sections.summary: Feedback will be consolidated into a Celebrating SG Families Plan, to be unveiled at the CIFA Regional Symposium & MSF Asian Family Conference 2022 in November.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The feedback will be consolidated into a Celebrating SG Families Plan, which will set out our society's commitment and support for families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will unveil the Plan at the CIFA Regional Symposium & MSF Asian Family Conference 2022, in November.

sections.label: Couples benefiting from programme
sections.summary: Today, more than 14,500 couples have benefited from this programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, more than 14,500 couples have benefited from this programme.

sections.label: MSF dedicates 2022 to families
sections.summary: MSF will dedicate 2022 as the Year of Celebrating SG Families to rally Singaporeans in celebrating families' important role.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To rally Singaporeans in celebrating the important role that families play in our lives, I am pleased to announce that MSF will dedicate 2022 as the "Year of Celebrating SG Families" (YCF).

sections.label: Challenges facing some families
sections.summary: Some families face complex, deep-seated and interlocking challenges that cannot be resolved by one agency, partner or social worker alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But some families face an array of challenges that may prevent them from seizing the opportunities in front of them – debt and financial difficulties, health problems, job instability, children struggling in school, family conflict, mindset barriers, housing insecurity, mental health issues and more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These are often complex, deep-seated and interlocking, unlike the kinds of difficulties that most families face from time to time, and they cannot be resolved by one Government agency, community partner, one social worker or on its own.

sections.label: 3Cs approach to support
sections.summary: The 3Cs approach provides Comprehensive, Convenient and Coordinated support, and transformation work started a few years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The transformation will take time and we have already started work a few years ago; improving inter-agency processes and officers' capabilities, building systems and enabling platforms and, importantly, strengthening and building relationships of trust within local networks on the ground to provide holistic support to families in need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We call this our "3C"s approach, which we have shared in Parliament over the last few years – providing Comprehensive, Convenient and Coordinated support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Comprehensive – in addressing presenting issues, as well as deeper root causes; Convenient support – so that families can focus their energies on improving their lives; and Coordinated – across different agencies and partners.

sections.label: Streamlined Assessment Protocols for ComCare
sections.summary: Streamlined Assessment Protocols let ComCare families access different support forms based on one means-testing assessment, across six agencies so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But she may need other assistance, too, for example, support with school fees for her children, from MOE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, we have set up what we call Streamlined Assessment Protocols, or SAPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These allow ComCare families to easily access different forms of support based on just one means-testing assessment, rather than being assessed separately for each scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have done this across six agencies so far, covering schemes on digital access, rental housing, healthcare, education and childcare.

sections.label: Further streamlining for ComCare families
sections.summary: The process will be further streamlined so eligible ComCare families automatically receive help from relevant schemes without additional applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Leon Perera will be glad to know that we will further streamline this process, so that eligible ComCare families automatically receive help from the relevant schemes, doing away with additional applications for each scheme.

sections.label: Automatic MOE Financial Assistance
sections.summary: By the end of the second quarter of this year, ComCare clients with children in Government or Government-aided schools will automatically receive MOE Financial Assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: By the end of the second quarter of this year, ComCare clients like Mrs Tan, whose children are in Government or Government-aided schools, will automatically receive MOE Financial Assistance, without needing to apply at their children's schools.

sections.label: Automatic CHAS referrals
sections.summary: By the end of 2022, eligible ComCare clients will be automatically referred for CHAS, with 30,000 families expected to benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For instance, by the end of 2022, eligible ComCare clients will be automatically referred for the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) for medical and dental subsidies at participating clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We expect 30,000 ComCare families to benefit from the schemes bundle that we will progressively roll out.

sections.label: ComLink nationwide scale-up
sections.summary: Families work with agencies on action plans, and ComLink will be scaled up nationwide to support over 14,000 families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Throughout this process, the family is working with us on their action plans and taking greater charge of their future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We announced during last year's COS that we will scale up ComLink nationwide to support over 14,000 families over the next few years.

sections.label: SSO officers as coordinators
sections.summary: SSO officers coordinate other agencies and align their efforts and programmes around the family's common plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: SSO officers then serve as overall coordinator, pulling in other agencies to support the family where necessary and aligning agencies' efforts and their schemes and programmes around the family's common plan.

sections.label: Scaling up befrienders pilot
sections.summary: Befrienders build trust with families, so the pilot will be scaled up this year, with MSF assessing all befrienders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But more importantly, families and befrienders have the opportunity to develop trust and deeper relationships and the families are often more motivated to follow through on their plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, scale up the pilot this year to support more ComLink families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Many of these befrienders are referred to us by community partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And MSF interviews and conducts suitability assessments on all befrienders.

sections.label: Consolidating common systems centrally
sections.summary: Common systems and processes across agencies, such as a database and volunteer training system, will be consolidated and managed centrally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For instance, they need a database to support the families' progress and a system to train and manage volunteers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, try to consolidate some of these common systems and processes across agencies and manage them centrally.

sections.label: MSFCare Network volunteering invitation
sections.summary: Everyone is invited to join the MSFCare Network, launched by Minister Masagos Zulkifli, for volunteering and giving opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We need all the help that we can get.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We invite everyone to join the MSFCare Network, which Minister Masagos Zulkifli launched earlier this year, to explore volunteering and giving opportunities and connect with like-minded people in making a difference to our society.

sections.label: Year of Celebrating SG Families
sections.summary: Parenting programmes and the FFLC initiative are described, and 2022 will be designated the Year of Celebrating SG Families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since 2014, about 58,000 parents have benefited from our evidence-based parenting programmes in MOE Primary and Secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2021, we started the Families for Life @ Community initiative (FFLC), in Nee Soon Central and Choa Chu Kang, to bring these programmes into the community so that more families can benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Building on MSF's sustained efforts to strengthen families, we will designate 2022 as the Year of Celebrating SG Families (YCF).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Families for Life (FFL) will continue to disseminate the "Family and Me" preschool resource packages to cultivate an appreciation of family from a young age and nurture family values through family songs, activities and big books.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We expanded this to around 50% of preschools last year and will reach out to remaining preschools by 2025.

sections.label: Benefits for Singaporean families
sections.summary: The Government provides broad-based benefits to support children's development regardless of parents' marital status, listing schemes such as MediSave Grants and Baby Bonus CDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government provides Singaporean families with broad-based benefits to support their children's development, regardless of their parents' marital status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: They are MediSave Grants for Newborns, MediShield Life Coverage, Infant Care Subsidy, Childcare Subsidy, Foreign Domestic Worker Levy Concession, education subsidies, healthcare subsidies, Baby Bonus Children Development Account (CDA), including CDA First Step, Childcare Leave, Unpaid Infant Care Leave, Maternity Leave and Adoption Leave.

sections.label: Family violence enquiries and recommendations
sections.summary: Enquiries and new cases rose from FY2018 to FY2020, and the Government accepted in principle all 16 Taskforce on Family Violence recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For instance, there were 2,906 enquiries in FY2018, of which 891 new cases were taken up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In FY2020, there were 4,574 enquiries, of which 1,103 new cases were taken up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted, in principle, all 16 recommendations from the Taskforce on Family Violence which Mr Melvin Yong had asked about.

sections.label: Full-day preschool places doubled
sections.summary: Full-day preschool places more than doubled in the past decade, from 90,000 in 2012 to around 200,000 as of end-2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The number of full-day preschool places has more than doubled in the past decade – from 90,000 places in 2012 to around 200,000 as of end-2021.

sections.label: Preschool places by 2025
sections.summary: By around 2025, eight in 10 preschoolers can have a place in Government-supported preschools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: By around 2025, eight in 10 preschoolers can have a place in our Government-supported preschools.

sections.label: Early childhood educators increased
sections.summary: Plans will further raise the quality of early childhood professionals and programmes, and educators increased from 18,000 in 2018 to over 23,000 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Today, I will be sharing our plans to further raise the quality of early childhood professionals and programmes, to complement parental guidance at home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have increased the number of early childhood educators from 18,000 in 2018 to over 23,000 last year.

sections.label: Leadership Development Framework introduced
sections.summary: A Leadership Development Framework (LDF) is being introduced to the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Today, it is my pleasure to announce the introduction of a Leadership Development Framework (LDF) to the sector.

sections.label: Quality Teaching Tool development
sections.summary: A new Quality Teaching Tool is being developed to raise teaching quality and encourage sharing of good practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will also do more to raise the quality of teaching and encourage the sharing of good teaching practices across the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that we are developing a new Quality Teaching Tool.

sections.label: Learning Communities future leaders
sections.summary: Learning Community members will be nurtured as future curriculum and pedagogical leaders, leading Communities of Practice for some 300 early childhood educators in two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Members of these Learning Communities will be nurtured to become future curriculum and pedagogical leaders, and to lead Communities of Practice to benefit some 300 early childhood educators within the next two years.

sections.label: Private intervention providers increase
sections.summary: ECDA will increase Enhanced Pilot for Private Intervention Providers programme providers from 10 to 16.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: ECDA will also increase the number of providers under the Enhanced Pilot for Private Intervention Providers, or PPIP programme, from 10 to 16.

sections.label: Early childhood and KidSTART support
sections.summary: Professional development, a Quality Teaching Tool, a framework review, and nationwide KidSTART scale-up from 2023 will support early childhood professionals, children and lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To do so, we will support the professional development of early childhood professionals and develop a Quality Teaching Tool to raise the quality of teaching.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will also review the Early Years Development Framework to support educators in creating enriching learning experiences for our children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To provide more support to children in lower-income families, we will progressively scale up KidSTART nationwide from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This will equip parents and caregivers with the knowledge and skills to support their children's well-being and development.

sections.label: Job, training and disability support
sections.summary: 1,700 new job and training opportunities were created, JGI supported over 2,900 persons with disabilities, and Day Activity Centre funding rose by $3 million.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For example, 1,700 new job and training opportunities were created last year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This includes opportunities from the new Place-and-Train and Attach-and-Train programmes, which we will extend to December this year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) has supported over 2,900 persons with disabilities between September 2020 and August 2021, which MOM will extend to September 2022 this year as well.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In October 2021, we increased funding for Day Activity Centres (DACs) by $3 million, or 20%.

sections.label: ATF beneficiaries income data
sections.summary: From April 2019 to December 2021, the ATF benefited close to 7,000 persons, with 66% from households with per capita income of $800 or less.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From April 2019 to December 2021, the ATF benefited close to 7,000 persons, with 66% of beneficiaries from households with a per capita income of $800 or less.

sections.label: Food cost support for low-income households
sections.summary: Low-income households are helped with supermarket, hawker and merchant purchases via grocery, CDC and HSP vouchers, and ComCare rates cover food needs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We have helped low-income households to defray the cost of purchases at supermarkets, hawker centres and heartland merchants.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This includes grocery vouchers for eligible households in 2020 and Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers in 2021 and as part of the Household Support Package (HSP) in Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: ComCare cash assistance rates, which are regularly reviewed, take into account food-related expenditures based on the Health Promotion Board's nutritional guidelines to ensure that families can meet their nutritional needs.

sections.label: Coordinating food support ecosystem
sections.summary: MSF engages food support organisations and partners, convened the Charity Food Workgroup in 2019, and soft-launched the FoodConnect directory and database.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: MSF has been actively engaging food support organisations and community partners to coordinate food support.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We convened the Charity Food Workgroup in 2019 to co-create a more responsive and coordinated food support ecosystem with different stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In February this year, we soft-launched the FoodConnect directory and database.

sections.label: Reaching out to ComLink families
sections.summary: Families are proactively reached upstream to understand their needs, strengths and aspirations, with over 6,800 ComLink families reached so far.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: First, we proactively reach out to families upstream to understand their needs, strengths and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We have reached out to more than 6,800 ComLink families so far.

sections.label: Career Advice and Mentoring Programme
sections.summary: CAMP, co-designed with MOE and ITE and partnered with Trybe Limited, supports youths leaving ITE early, with 14 mentors and 10 youths since January.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Co-designed with MOE and ITE, and in partnership with Trybe Limited, our Career Advice and Mentoring Programme (CAMP) will expand networks of positive relationships for youths who leave ITE prematurely and empower them to achieve their aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Since its launch in January this year, 14 mentors and 10 youths have come on board and more are expected to join in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Over the two years' pilot, we aim to support 100 youths.

sections.label: Lasting Power of Attorney registrations
sections.summary: As of 2021, about 130,000 Singapore Citizens, or about 4% of eligible adult citizens, have registered their LPAs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As of 2021, about 130,000 Singapore Citizens, or about 4% of all eligible adult citizens, have registered their LPAs.

sections.label: Deputyship court orders
sections.summary: In the past five years there were 2,794 Court orders appointing deputies, growing at about 25% annually.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: On deputyship, there were 2,794 Court orders appointing deputies in the past five years, with the number growing at about 25% annually.

sections.label: Mentoring programme for ITE leavers
sections.summary: A two-year pilot mentoring programme aims to support 100 youths who leave ITE prematurely.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Last year, we announced a pilot mentoring programme for students who leave ITE prematurely.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We hope that this programme will empower them to achieve their aspirations with a positive mindset.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We aim to support 100 youths over the two-year pilot.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: (In English): To conclude, Madam, MSF has spoken about the suite of policies and programmes to support families with different needs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will continue to work with the community to build resilient individuals, strong families and a caring society.

sections.label: Inter-ethnic marriages share doubled
sections.summary: Inter-ethnic marriages rose from one in 10 over 30 years ago to almost one in five today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: More than 30 years ago, one in 10 of all marriages were inter-ethnic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Today, it is doubled – almost one in five.

sections.label: Survey on same-sex relations attitudes
sections.summary: An IPS survey showed 11.4% of respondents felt same-sex relations were not wrong, double the 2013 figure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In fact, an IPS survey in 2019 showed that while small, 11.4% of the respondents felt that sexual relations between two same-sex adults were not wrong at all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This is still double the figure in 2013, which was about 5.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But while societal attitudes are gradually shifting, the majority value and wish to preserve the traditional family – that of a man and a woman marrying and raising the child or children in a stable family unit.

sections.label: Support for single unwed parents
sections.summary: MSF is following up on pain points of single unwed parents, including childminding and employment support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Specifically, for the areas which we are following up on in our dialogues and engagement sessions with single unwed parents, a few areas, a few pain points, have been highlighted to us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: That is why, in my main response earlier, I had talked about the childminding service pilot that MSF will be partnering a social service agency to provide childminding service beyond a regular childcare centre's operating hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The second area – when it comes to employment support, we are having discussions with NTUC, with community partners, to see what are the areas we can assist our single unwed parents in, be it in training or finding local opportunities for these single parents to be able to re-enter the workforce and get on a sustainable path with their children.

sections.label: Rental flat application outcomes
sections.summary: Single unwed parents generally receive rental flat application outcomes within three weeks of submitting required information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Members will recall that Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim had recently shared in Parliament that, generally, single unwed parents can receive the outcome of their rental flat application within three weeks of submitting all required information, although additional time may be required for complex cases.

sections.label: ComLink expansion to more towns
sections.summary: ComLink, piloted at four sites in 2019, is expanding through a two-phased approach to 11 towns then 10 towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: But I do think it is a little bit premature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We started ComLink with four sites in 2019 – Jalan Kukoh, Boon Lay, Kembangan-Chai Chee as well as Marsiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, we have piloted that at four sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We thought the model worked well and that is why we are going into a two-phased approach: 11 towns last year, as well as 10 towns this year.

sections.label: Funding for disability services
sections.summary: Funding for day activity centres rose about 20% or $3 million, and adult disability home funding rose about 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: For instance, I mentioned increased funding for our day activity centres by some 20% or $3 million last year and we have also increased funding for our adult disability homes by about 25% most recently as well.

sections.label: Results of study later
sections.summary: The results and findings will be made known in the later part of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: As Members know now, the results and findings of which will be made known in the later part of this year.

sections.label: MOE spending on adults
sections.summary: MOE spends about $260 million a year, with more cohorts coming and many adults without services now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MOE, I computed, spends about $260 million a year – there are some more cohorts coming and there are a lot of adults who do not have services now.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan 2030 goals
sections.summary: The speaker co-chairs with Mr Gan Seow Kee and the EMP sets tangible goals leading up to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I am co-chairing that with Mr Gan Seow Kee, Vice-Chairman of SBF, and I think that is a good example of how we hope to really make a difference in this disability space for good and in a sustained fashion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And in this latest EMP, one of the bold moves that we are making – and I am letting the cat out of the bag a little bit here – is to really fix some tangible goals for ourselves as to where we want to get to in the next few years leading up to 2030, where the endpoint of the Enabling Masterplan is.

sections.label: Digital literacy and ComCare access
sections.summary: The Member asks about bridging the digital literacy gap and empowering ComLink befrienders with PDPA safeguards for ComCare applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I appreciate the Ministry's efforts to increase the digitalisation efforts to make financial assistance more accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But given that many of the vulnerable communities are very low on their digital literacy, where they literally may not even know how to use Gmail on their phones, let alone to navigate Government portals, I would like to know what are the Ministry's efforts in trying to bridge this digital literacy gap and, if the befrienders from ComLink are meant to also support them on this front, then what are the ways that the Ministry might be looking at empowering befrienders and giving them the necessary access and safeguards around PDPA to support ComCare beneficiaries for their online applications?

sections.label: ComCare support and discretion
sections.summary: SSOs have discretion to continue support after a person finds a better job, avoiding a cliff effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We are not there to kick people out of ComCare or get them out of ComCare because we just do not want to give them support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We want to enable them and, as mentioned in my speech, if Ms Carrie Tan has heard carefully, the SSOs are given discretion to continue support even after the person has found, for example, a job, a better job, a better paying job, and not suffer this cliff effect that we may have, inadvertently, through our policy, done in the past.

sections.label: Focus on 14,000 identified families
sections.summary: The speaker says to focus on the 14,000 families already identified, as each needs a bespoke and customised approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: First, on expanding beyond the existing pool that we have identified to include those from self-help groups, schools, FAS and whatnot, I am mindful that we already have 14,000 families identified for this year and the next.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I would say that let us focus on these 14,000 families because a bespoke and customised approach has to be had for each of these families.

sections.label: Co-location of SSOs and FSCs
sections.summary: Co-location of institutions such as SSOs and FSCs was piloted at Kreta Ayer and Bukit Merah, co-locating the SSO and FST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The third question relates to the co-location of the different institutions, SSOs, FSCs and all that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We have piloted that at Kreta Ayer and Bukit Merah and we have co-located the SSO and FST.

sections.label: Preschool places in Dawson
sections.summary: ECDA planned new centres and extensions of existing centres in the Dawson area to increase preschool places for rising demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second clarification, can the Ministry consider my proposal to have active reach-outs to families which have been on the waiting list for about three to six months?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With the injection of new BTOs in the Dawson area, Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has planned new centres, as well as extension of existing centres, to increase preschool places to address the increase in demand.

sections.label: Income mobility estimates for Singapore
sections.summary: Chetty et al 2014 authors updated estimates using administrative data; Singapore's share reaching the top income quintile is about 14%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The source is Chetty et al, 2014, and the authors are from the US, UK, Denmark; and our own estimates are updated by the authors using administrative data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The US is about 7.5% for the share of individuals who reach the top income quintile among those born to the bottom quintile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In Singapore, it is maintained at about 14%, especially for those that we have estimated for the 1985 to 1989 cohorts.

sections.label: Criticism of $1,600 income measure
sections.summary: The $1,600 monthly income call includes private enrichment classes, jewellery and perfume, so it does not reflect basic necessity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For example, the call for $1,600 monthly income for a single or partnered household includes private enrichment classes, jewellery, perfume and therefore, in no way reflects what should be, at least, the basic necessity that we should meet for needy income households.

sections.label: Motion to reduce Head I Estimates
sections.summary: The Member moves that the total sum allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sections.label: Single parent parity and demographic trends
sections.summary: The passage argues for parity for single parents, notes demographic trends, and calls for more incentives for singles caring for ageing parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For many years, together with other Members of the House, we have argued for parity in treatment of single parents, especially single mothers, as a parent of equal standing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We are seeing some demographic trends including increasing singlehood, declining fertility rates and an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We need to consider more incentives, for example, for singles who have ageing parents, since caregiving duties fall most heavily on them.

sections.label: Promoting and strengthening families
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry what it is doing to promote and strengthen families and asks the Minister to outline changing trends and policy implications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Ministry what it is doing to promote and to strengthen families so that we can be a more resilient society?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can the Minister also outline some changing trends and the implications for our various social and fiscal policies?

sections.label: Loss of human connections
sections.summary: The passage states that as a doctor the speaker sees middle-aged people develop cognitive and physical dysfunction, forgetfulness, loneliness, poor sleep and fear of going out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my work as a doctor, I see the fallout from this loss of human connections.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many middle-aged people develop cognitive and physical dysfunction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many reported being more forgetful, lonelier and sleeping poorly, and expressed they fear going out.

sections.label: Job loss and COVID-19 measures
sections.summary: The passage states some lost jobs, healthcare workers worked without breaks, school closures required adaptation, and many school-going children received Health Risk Notices and need daily ART swabs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some have lost their jobs, some in healthcare have worked non-stop without a break for months; and every time there was a school closure, we have to figure out how to adapt.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Now, so many school-going children have received the Health Risk Notice (HRN) and need to do daily ART swabs.

sections.label: COVID-19 mental health and familial gatherings
sections.summary: The passage states COVID-19's adverse impact on mental health is well reported and asks to consider allowing familial gatherings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The adverse impact of COVID-19 on our nation’s mental health is well reported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask for a simplistic solution: consider allowing familial gatherings.

sections.label: Old-age dependency and family strains
sections.summary: The passage states the old-age dependency ratio rose from 13.5 to 23.4 in 10 years and that increasing singlehood, declining fertility and ageing can strain families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lastly, the old-age dependency ratio has drastically increased from 13.5 to 23.4 in the same 10-year period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These trends of increasing singlehood, declining fertility rates and a rapidly ageing population can place additional strains on our families across different life stages.

sections.label: Lower-income family relationship vulnerability
sections.summary: The lower-income group is most vulnerable to strained family relationships due to limited resources to support one another.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The lower-income group remains the most vulnerable to fallouts from strained family relationships because of the limited resources among family members to support one another.

sections.label: Alliance for Action initiatives
sections.summary: The Ministry launched the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships in August last year, and asks about new initiatives in six areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, the Ministry launched the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships in August last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What would be the new initiatives in the six areas of focus – newlywed couples, parents, single parents, families with early risks, marriages and families among different religious faiths, and families in general?

sections.label: Baby Bonus cash component denial
sections.summary: The passage asks why the cash component of the Baby Bonus is denied to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Why deny them the cash component of the Baby Bonus?

sections.label: Single unwed parents cash support
sections.summary: With a median salary of $600 a month, the cash component would help single unwed parents under 35, and core inflation is projected at 2% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With a median salary of only $600 a month, the cash component would really help single unwed parents under 35 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Everyone will also face higher living costs, with core inflation projected to be 2% to 3% this year.

sections.label: Nanny services for single parents
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MSF will establish a pilot programme of low-cost, ad hoc nanny services for single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MSF establish a pilot programme of providing low-cost, ad hoc nanny services for our single unwed parents?

sections.label: Family violence cases during pandemic
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MSF has seen an increase in family violence cases received by Family Violence Specialist Centres since the pandemic started.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Has MSF seen an increase in the number of family violence cases received by the Family Violence Specialist Centres since the start of the pandemic?

sections.label: Singapore Women's Development Conversations
sections.summary: The Conversations on Singapore Women's Development concluded in September last year, with 160 conversations involving over 5,700 participants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development were concluded in September last year, with the Government promising concrete proposals in three areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: What stood out for me was the engagement of many Singaporeans through these conversations, all 160 of them, involving more than 5,700 participants.

sections.label: Adoption of Children Act review
sections.summary: The Ministry announced a review of the Adoption of Children Act and sought public feedback on proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Last year, the Ministry announced that the Adoption of Children Act is being reviewed to better safeguard the welfare of adopted children and sought the public's feedback on the proposed amendments to the Act.

sections.label: Adoption review and waiting children
sections.summary: The passage asks about children waiting to be adopted, adoptive parents' profiles, Government help, and notes the review was motivated by international practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: How many children are waiting to be adopted, what is the profile of adoptive parents and the help rendered to these families by the Government?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Second, the review of the Act was motivated, in part, by the need for Singapore to keep pace with international practice.

sections.label: ECDA engagement on waiting vacancies
sections.summary: The passage asks if the Ministry can set a timeline for ECDA to engage parents and propose nearby centres with vacancies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry set a certain timeline where after a certain number of months of waiting and still no vacancy, ECDA should engage the parents, understand their needs and propose a few suitable nearby centres with vacancies for their selection and registration?

sections.label: KidSTART expansion nationwide
sections.summary: KidSTART was launched in the speaker's division in 2016, and the Prime Minister announced last year it will be expanded nationwide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: KidSTART was launched in my division in 2016 and I saw first-hand the difference that it has made and is still making.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome Prime Minister's announcement last year that KidSTART will be expanded nationwide.

sections.label: KidSTART studies and family benefits
sections.summary: The passage hopes for long-term studies tracking children and families in KidSTART and asks MSF about family benefits and the Growing Together with KidSTART initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I also hope that there could be long-term studies to review and track the progress of our children and their families in KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask MSF if it can share how families will benefit from the expansion of KidSTART and provide an update on the Growing Together with KidSTART initiative.

sections.label: Conditional cash transfer for absentees
sections.summary: Proposes a conditional cash transfer for persistently absent Primary and Secondary students, conditional on commitment to early intervention and regular attendance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For families where persistent absenteeism is an issue, I would like to propose a conditional cash transfer programme – not a transfer to the Child Development Account – for these students in Primary and Secondary schools conditional on their commitment to student early intervention programmes and regular school attendance.

sections.label: Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund
sections.summary: Since 2001, The Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund has given low-income students a monthly allowance conditional on school attendance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since 2001, The Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund has been providing a monthly allowance for students from low-income backgrounds conditional on school attendance.

sections.label: Single person scheme payments
sections.summary: A single person gets $600 a month and other help such as free healthcare, with 4,263 people on the scheme in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: A single person, he or she, gets $600 a month and other help, such as free healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: In 2020, there were 4,263 people on the scheme, 3% fewer than the year before.

sections.label: Social worker resignation and anxiety rates
sections.summary: In 2019 the social worker resignation rate was 17%, and a SUSS study found 57% had anxiety during the pandemic in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: In 2019, the overall annual resignation rate of social workers was 17%, which is double that of the estimated 8% attrition rate of healthcare workers in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: In a recent SUSS study, 57% of social workers were found to be suffering from anxiety during the pandemic in 2020.

sections.label: Aid for basic dignity and poverty
sections.summary: Calls for enough aid for basic dignity relative to minimum wage benchmarks and inflation, and to break the poverty cycle for children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: What I am calling for is enough aid for the basic dignity of the poor relative to minimum wage benchmarks and inflation and based on the latest research; enough aid to break the poverty cycle for the children; and with aid delivered in such a way that it drives better outcomes.

sections.label: ComLink reaching rental households
sections.summary: MSF announced that over the next two years ComLink will reach rental households with children and young people across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MSF has announced that, over the course of the next two years, ComLink will reach rental households with children and young people all across Singapore.

sections.label: Upscaling benefits rental housing families
sections.summary: Upscaling efforts are expected to benefit 14,000 families with children living in rental housing across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Notably, the upscaling efforts are expected to benefit 14,000 families with children living in rental housing across Singapore.

sections.label: ComLink expansion progress update request
sections.summary: MSF is asked for an update on ComLink's expansion, the number of families assisted, and how frequently check-ins are conducted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Having said that, could MSF provide an update on the progress of ComLink's expansion?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Could MSF elaborate on the number of families it has assisted through ComLink so far and outline how frequently are check-ins conducted with the families?

sections.label: Food aid coordination and integration
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked about integration of assistance services, and the Government is proposed to coordinate food aid by expanding the Community Shop concept.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry share an update on how the integration of assistance services for these families is progressing?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, a recent study estimated that 10% of resident households were food insecure in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Food distribution drives do important work but may be fragmented and lead to food wastage if rations are unsuitable due to health preference or dietary reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I propose that the Government coordinate food aid by expanding the Community Shop concept of public rental flats and pockets of low-income family areas island-wide.

sections.label: Preferred food programme respondents
sections.summary: Ninety-eight percent of respondents selected it as their preferred type of food programme after the first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Ninety-eight percent of respondents selected it as their preferred type of food programme after the first year.

sections.label: Streamlining processes for ComLink families
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider streamlining processes so families need not spend so much effort on administration matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Such regular sharing has been very effective in providing timely help to these families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Therefore, I welcome the announcement by Minister Lawrence Wong to scale up Community Link or ComLink.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider streamlining all these processes so that they need not spend so much effort on administration matters and instead focus on improving their situation?

sections.label: Court orders appointing deputies 2021
sections.summary: Based on Office of the Public Guardian data, only 873 Court orders appointing deputies were received in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Based on data from the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG), only 873 Court orders appointing deputies were received in 2021.

sections.label: Next Enabling Masterplan for Disabled
sections.summary: Singapore's next Enabling Masterplan for the Disabled is being made and will expire in 2030, eight years later than earlier five-year plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore’s next Enabling Masterplan for the Disabled (EMP4) is in the making.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Unlike earlier plans which lasted for five years, this one will expire in 2030, eight years later.

sections.label: Funding for disability services
sections.summary: There must be a computation of what disability services would cost to meet basic and aspirational goals, and MSF ought to be better funded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the national level, there must at least be a computation of what disability services would cost to meet basic and then aspirational goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MSF ought to be better funded in the national budget for these critical essentials.

sections.label: EMP4 Executive Council and schemes
sections.summary: An EMP4 Executive Council should be set up to report and review yearly and at milestones, and MSF announced expansion of SMF and ATF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Five, set up a EMP4 Executive Council to report and review the EMP4 yearly after the Masterplan is published and to report and review at specific milestones or during major changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is naive to think that an eight-year Masterplan would still be relevant in 2030 if we start with just a plan now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Government has paid a lot of attention but needs are getting complex and multiplying.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Including the disabled is an important chapter of a Singapore Story that will make us truly human, caring and inclusive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In January, the MSF announced an expansion of the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF) as well as the Assistive Technology Fund (ATF).

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Amongst others, the existing schemes will be extended to support seniors and the disabled over a longer period of time and to cover a wider range of assistive devices.

sections.label: ATF enhancements for citizens only
sections.summary: Annex B of the MSF January press release says ATF enhancements will only apply to Singapore Citizens, with no changes for PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Annex B of the MSF January press release contains a noteworthy footnote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It says that the enhancements to ATF will only apply the Singapore Citizens while there will be no changes to benefits for PRs.

sections.label: Waiting list for centres
sections.summary: The passage asks how many individuals are currently on the waiting list for these centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How many individuals are on the waiting list for these centres currently?

sections.label: Funding for adult disability care
sections.summary: Ageing parents often bear caregiving fully, and MSF is called to fund adult disability care facilities at least on par with SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a result, their ageing parents often have to bear the full weight of caregiving and many worry about how their children will be cared for after they pass on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would like to call for MSF to enhance its funding and support for the adult disability care facilities to be at least on par with what SPED schools receive.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplans since 2007
sections.summary: MSF has charted three Enabling Masterplans since 2007, achieving changes in infrastructure, policies, support and attitudes, with a new edition charting a roadmap through 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Since 2007, MSF has charted three Enabling Masterplans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These Masterplans have not only achieved material changes in infrastructure, policies and support for persons with disabilities but have seeped these changes into the attitudes of fellow Singaporeans, including educators, employers and the public at large.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is with great anticipation that we look forward to this new edition of the Enabling Masterplan which I understand takes a longer view than previous iterations charting a roadmap through 2030.

sections.label: Reaching caregivers of persons with disabilities
sections.summary: MSF is invited to consider better reaching caregivers whose charges have undiagnosed or unreported disabilities and to assess informational gaps from digital divide or language barriers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Although previous iterations on the Enabling Masterplans have indeed sought to alleviate the worries of caregivers in future care planning, I invite the MSF to consider how we can better reach out to caregivers like Mdm Tan with many going under the radar due to their charges undiagnosed or unreported disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Also, I invite the MSF to assess informational gaps faced by caregivers of adults with disabilities perhaps due to digital divide or language barriers so that we can better build bridges to alleviate the concerns of these caregivers.

sections.label: Work opportunities for PWDs above 18
sections.summary: MSF is asked whether it plans to support persons with disabilities above age 18 with work opportunities and services to stay meaningfully engaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to ask if MSF has plans to support PWDs above the age of 18 with work opportunities and services so that they may stay meaningfully engaged.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan 2030 details requested
sections.summary: The member seeks further details on the Enabling Masterplan 2030 and strategic efforts to bring in stakeholders and community to support caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am grateful for the Government's various efforts including engaging different stakeholders through focus group discussions and working with partners and charities to enhance services and funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am appreciative of the ongoing efforts and I am heartened to hear that we will be launching the Enabling Masterplan 2030 to further strengthen support in areas like employment, lifelong learning and respite care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could I get further details on the Enabling Masterplan and the strategic effort to bring in different stakeholders and the community to provide different dimensions of support to the caregivers?

sections.label: Mentoring programme progress update
sections.summary: MSF is asked for a progress update on the mentoring programme, how many mentors and mentees were recruited, and what success might look like.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MSF provide a progress update on the mentoring programme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: How many mentors and mentees have been recruited thus far and what might success look like, at the end of the programme?

sections.label: Mentoring programme pilot for youths
sections.summary: The Minister is asked for an update on the mentoring programme pilot for youths, its benefits to participants, and numbers on its size and impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: At last year's COS, the Ministry announced the mentoring programme pilot for youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update of the progress of this pilot and how it will benefit the youths who have participated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Can the Minister also provide some numbers as to the size and impact of the programme?

sections.label: Support for social workers
sections.summary: Nearly 60% of frontline social workers had anxiety and 45% depression during the pandemic, prompting calls to improve programmes and launch the Community Capacity Trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Despite all these programmes, nearly 60% of frontline social workers were affected by anxiety at the height of the pandemic, with 45% facing depression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Let us focus on what more we can do for social workers, by improving our existing programmes and launching new initiatives like the Community Capacity Trust, by moving beyond guidelines and helping FSCs implement these programmes and use the grants provided.
